text:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — we need one aligned plan for the Hosted API slice for the next quarter. Major asks from customers: tighter embeddings SLA, a lightweight rerank API for search teams, and lower chat p95 for small-memory models. Can we lay out scope tradeoffs and clear launch criteria?

Dan Patel: +1. My take: we can't do full rerank SLA and embeddings low-latency guarantees in the same sprint without cutting something else. Need to pick priorities.

Leo Rivera: For runtime improvements I can scope three workstreams: 1) prefix/KV microcache (low risk, good p95 wins), 2) batching improvements (medium risk, big cost impact), 3) model-variant routing (higher risk). Which two do we commit?

Anna Novak: From model side: embeddings latency depends a lot on quantization and IO. We can push a quantized embedding runtime path but it adds ~2 weeks of QA. Rerank can be implemented as a thin scoring endpoint that calls existing encoders + a lightweight dot product; lower scope if we force single-model support at launch.

Sam O'Neill: Customers pushing for rerank pilot are willing to sign short-term paid pilot if we can promise <100ms median for 512-d embeddings and a guarantees doc. But they expect example backfills and sample prompts.

Katie Park: CS signals: three enterprise accounts asked for per-route SLOs and a clear rollback plan. They don't need fully dedicated capacity yet — just predictable degraded behavior and an ETA if we hit errors.

Maria Chen: Proposal: split into two launch slices this quarter — "Performance Baseline" and "Rerank Pilot". Performance Baseline = KV cache + batching opt + embedding quantized path. Rerank Pilot = thin scoring API + sample integration + canary customers. Drop model-variant routing for this quarter. Thoughts?

Dan Patel: That seems reasonable. If we drop model-variant routing, we free ~3 dev-weeks on infra -> use for robust canary infra and fallback hooks. Also want to add a small feature: per-route rate-limiting knob for pilots.

Leo Rivera: Agree. Order of work: KV cache (2w) -> batching (3w) -> quantized embedding path (2w testing). We should spike on canary orchestration in parallel (1w). Parallel work will need 2 engineers for runtime, 1 for infra.

Anna Novak: For rerank pilot: limit to a single model family (e.g., small bi-encoder) and expose a /v1/rerank endpoint with an optional "top_k" param. We'll validate quality with a small eval set from Sam's pilot customers. Launch criteria for rerank pilot: 1) p95 <= 200ms for scored queries under baseline load, 2) precision@10 >= baseline threshold (TBD), 3) automated fallback to host ranking if error.

Sam O'Neill: I'll gather pilot agreements and two eval datasets. We should include an NDA checkbox on the pilot sign-up page.

Katie Park: Customer-facing checklist: docs, sample code (curl + node), runbook for oncall, rollback playbook, and a short SLA doc stating pilot expectations. If any of these are missing, customers won't sign.

Maria Chen: Good call. Let's write concrete launch criteria across both slices. Draft below, please comment inline: 

Performance Baseline launch criteria:
- Latency: chat p95 <= 250ms for short-turn chats (<=64 tokens) on hosted small model family.
- Embeddings: median <= 120ms and p95 <= 300ms for 768-d embeddings on standard plan.
- Stability: <1% error rate during 24h smoke test.
- Observability: per-route token cost + latency charts in Console + alerts for p95 and error rate.
- Rollout: staged canary across 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback.

Rerank Pilot launch criteria:
- API: /v1/rerank exists with top_k, return scores + normalized ranks.
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for scoring under pilot load.
- Quality: initial precision@10 >= customer-provided baseline OR not worse than current vendor by >5% (we'll define baseline per pilot).
- Customer readiness: at least 1 signed pilot + integration test from their infra.
- Safety: rate limits, auth, and data retention notes documented.

Dan Patel: Need to add "cost guardrails": throttling for heavy rerank calls and a default max_top_k = 50 to prevent runaway billing. Also a flag for customers to opt into cheaper approximate scoring (if we ship later).

Leo Rivera: For canary plan, suggest this rollout snippet (infra skeleton):

```yaml
canary:
  steps: [5, 25, 100]
  hold_for: 30m
  metrics: [p95_latency, error_rate, cpu_util]
  rollback_if: error_rate > 1% OR p95 > target * 1.25
```

Maria Chen: Love it. Who owns what? Proposed owners: Performance Baseline: Dan (eng), Leo (runtime), Anna (models). Rerank Pilot: Anna (lead on API), Dan (infra/canary), Sam (pilot customers), Katie (CS comms).

Anna Novak: I'll scope the embedding quant path RFC this week and drop a PR with perf numbers.

Dan Patel: I'll book 3 sprint tasks: kv-cache spike, batching perf, canary infra. ETA for first spike results by EOW.

Sam O'Neill: I'll confirm the pilot customer tomorrow and share dataset + contact.

Katie Park: I'll prepare the customer checklist doc and a short FAQ for pilot expectations.

DeployBot: Deployment scheduled: none (manual canary to be triggered after tests). :robot_face: 

Maria Chen: Thanks team — action items: Dan + Leo finalize slotting (capacity) by Monday, Anna submit RFC for embedding path by Thurs, Sam confirm pilot customer, Katie draft checklist. We'll regroup next Tue 10am. :calendar: 

Leo Rivera: One last tradeoff note — if a customer demands sub-100ms p95 for embeddings, we should propose Dedicated capacity or a model-variant path next quarter. Let's call that out explicitly in sales docs to set expectations.

Maria Chen: Agreed. Call that out in the pilot FAQ. Closing thread: please add any blockers now, otherwise we'll run with these owners. :thumbsup:
